title: separate-lease-heartbeat-and-backpressure-smoothing-for-continuous-batcher
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The continuous batching pipeline currently couples KV lease heartbeats with the batcher backpressure smoothing loop. This coupling causes periodic latency spikes when lease maintenance work aligns with heavy admission events, and it makes it difficult to reason about backpressure signals in the scheduler.

Goal: Refactor so lease heartbeat/renewal work is performed by an isolated lease manager with its own pacing, and expose a deterministic backpressure smoothing primitive that the scheduler and batcher can use without being blocked by KV maintenance. The change should reduce 95/99th token-latency spikes, simplify the scheduler codepath, and enable future optimizations (lease batching, prioritized lease renewal).

Scope:
- Extract lease heartbeat loop from continuous-batcher core into a LeaseManager component.
- Introduce a BackpressureSmoother interface with a small in-memory ring buffer to compute admission rate smoothing independently.
- Update scheduler to consume the smoother's smoothed admission rate rather than reading batcher-internal signals directly.
- Add metrics and tracing for lease churn, lease latency, smoother rate, and correlation with token latency.
- Add unit and integration tests; add canary rollout with runtime-1.20.

Non-goals: Rewriting eviction policies or changing KV storage layout. This ticket focuses on separation of concerns, not eviction heuristics.

Success criteria:
- 95th token latency reduced by >=10% on synthetic mixed chat workload with 128 token sequences.
- No regression in throughput for P99 concurrent sessions.
- Observability improvements (lease_renewals_sec, smoother_rate, lease_blocking_fraction) present in console dashboards.

Trade-offs and design notes:
- Moving heartbeats out of the batcher removes opportunistic renewals (when a batch touches a key) which could slightly raise renewal counts; we mitigate with lease batching and adaptive timers in LeaseManager.
- The BackpressureSmoother is intentionally lightweight to avoid adding GC churn; we use a ring buffer of ints and lock-free read path where possible.
- This increases the number of background goroutines per worker; we've budgeted 1 additional goroutine and added a pooled executor option for constrained environments.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/designs/runtime/lease-smoother-2026
- Perf dashboard (canary): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/runtime/lease-smoother-canary
- WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9842
comments: 2026-02-22 - Initial spike analysis: flamegraphs indicate 60% of tail spikes correlate with KV lease RPC retries during heavy admission bursts. Captured traces: trace-20260222-01. Ava.
2026-02-25 - Architecture review with infra & reliability. Decision: extract LeaseManager + opt-in Smoother API. Action items: create LeaseManager proto, add metrics contract. Liam.

2026-02-28 - Prototype implemented: LeaseManager extracted, smoother skeleton in place. Local synthetic benchmarks show 8% reduction in 95th latency, no throughput regression at 1000 concurrent sessions. Need CI perf runs. Liam.

2026-03-02 - Code review feedback from Priya (SRE): request adding lease renewal jitter and a histogram for lease_rpc_latency_ms. Also prefer token-bucket fallback if smoother fails. Filed PR comments. Priya.
2026-03-04 - Addressed review: added jitter, lease batching threshold, and histogram metrics. Added smoke integration tests for failure scenarios (lease RPC throttling). Liam.

2026-03-05 - Canary started on two dedicated pools (eu-west-1, us-west-2). Early results: 12% improvement p95 in eu-west-1, 6% in us-west-2. Observed one pod with increased lease renewal rate due to hot-key pattern; investigating hot-key mitigation. Ava.
Next steps: finish end-to-end canary, add rollout plan to console with automatic rollback if p95 increases >3% or error rate >0.5%.
Follow-ups: consider LeaseManager adaptive thresholds per-shard (future ticket).
